author: reek
body: The guest TCP stack survives a lossy or slow peer. This drives the pure NetworkStack -- no NIC, no emulator NAT -- so it tests the guest stack itself.

author: reek
body: A server session is brought to ESTABLISHED by a handshake (SYN, then a GET that rides in on the establishing ACK). Each test below starts from that same established session (referencing `established` re-runs the handshake, so the tests do not alias one shared session).

author: reek
body: RETRANSMISSION. The server sends a two-byte response, which arms the retransmit timer. With the outbox flushed and no ACK arriving, one tick leaves the outbox empty (rexmit1=0) and the third tick re-queues the response (rexmit3=1). A stack with no retransmission would show 0 at both -- the frame the peer missed would be gone. The control is the next test: an ACK that covers the response clears the stash, so three ticks re-queue nothing (acked3=0).

author: reek
body: RECEIVE WINDOW. A duplicate of already-delivered data (a lossy peer resending after losing our ACK) is dropped (dupdata=0), and so is a segment starting beyond the advertised window (windata=0); an in-order segment at recv-next is accepted (indata=1). Without the window check the duplicate and the out-of-window segment would both be delivered and corrupt the byte stream.

author: reek
body: TIME_WAIT. An active close reaches TIME_WAIT (twstate=TIME_WAIT); four ticks age it to CLOSED (afterwait=CLOSED) rather than leaving it for an external idle reclaim. Without aging it would sit in TIME_WAIT forever.
